resources.string: VFS path redirection for modules, without mounting anything.
This package ships no NoMount module for %1$s; use Automatic or Built-in Folk Mount.
The kernel carries NoMount %1$s but this build needs API 23 or newer; update the kernel.
The driver is not loaded yet; reboot or inject once to load it.
The kernel version could not be matched to a NoMount module.
Removes every redirection until the next reboot. Modules stop being injected.
The kernel refused the change. Check the driver state and try again.
Every app can see the injected files; pick apps below to hide them

The built-in Folk Mount hides injected files from apps whose profile says "unmount modules" (every non-root app by default). NoMount starts with no exclusions, so those apps see the files until you tick them here.
Copied from app profiles on demand
Isolated processes (WebView, SDK sandboxes) also see the stock filesystem.
Status unavailable. ksud must be up to date.
Tap a module to inject it now; the button on the right removes it until the next reboot.
Every app sees the injected files again.

Select the listed apps whose profile hides modules from them. The default profile hides them from every non-root app, so this usually selects almost all of them. Profiles are not tracked afterwards: change one and copy again.
Drops every rule and every exclusion until the next reboot.
The installed module %1$s drives the same driver; the built-in backend steps aside so only one of them writes rules.
Choose how modules are mounted on boot.
Unavailable. Root access is required and ksud must be up to date.
Use the metamodule when one is enabled, otherwise the built-in engine.
Always use the built-in Folk Mount engine.
Always let the metamodule handle mounting.
Inject modules through the NoMount VFS driver. Falls back to the built-in engine when the driver is unavailable.
Inject nothing. Installed modules stay inactive until a backend is selected.
An enabled metamodule is present; its scripts may not work with the built-in engine.
The NoMount driver is not answering; this boot falls back to the built-in engine.
The previous boot did not confirm NoMount UI readiness; this boot uses the Built-in engine. This does not prove a NoMount fault.
NoMount UI readiness was not confirmed; the next boot will use the Built-in engine.
A previous mount step did not finish; this boot skipped it to avoid repeating the same failure.
Failed to change the Folk Mount mode.

NoMount shows the injected files to every app at first; the built-in Folk Mount hides them from apps whose profile says \"unmount modules\" (every non-root app by default).\\n\\nSwitching takes effect after a reboot. To keep the old behaviour, tick the apps in NoMount → Excluded apps.
